problems: Merged rows: brazilian-republic holds Brazilian Republic, Unitary State of Brazil, Federated Republic of Brazil and Republic of Brazil (Q155, one republic since 15 November 1889); republic-of-cuba holds Republic of Cuba and Communist Cuba (Q241, official name unchanged). The slugs unitary-state-of-brazil, federated-republic-of-brazil, republic-of-brazil and communist-cuba (listed to other parts of am-08) must not get dossiers of their own, or the shapes would be reviewed twice; if a part has already written one, drop or alias it. Colour agent: one hue each.

mexico shares Q5062192 with centralist-mexico, but that id is the Centralist Republic's; mexico starts 15 July 1867 (Cliopatria 1868) as the continuation of federated-republic-of-mexico; new keyframes for 1867 and for 1913-1919 (Cliopatria has no Mexico shape in those years).

second-mexican-empire: Cliopatria's whole-country shape is a claim; the dossier draws the held land and mirrors the Federated Republic dossier's hatched occupation events; mexican-monarchists (am-08-g) is the 1864 Regency of the same regime and both draw 1864.
republic-of-colombia starts in 1886 (the United States of Colombia dossier keeps 1863-1886); Panama leaves on 3 November 1903 (split).

United States dossier (am-07) misreads Cliopatria's 8 US cells in Cuba in 1905-1907 and 1911-1925 as Guantánamo/Canal Zone: they are the Isle of Pines, handed to Cuba on 23 March 1925 (Hay-Quesada), an event its ledger lacks; it also lacks the Platt-Amendment client relation (vassal_start 1902 / vassal_end 1934).
